The ability to add digital driver's licenses to iPhone may soon expand to the 15th U.S. state.

Apple currently lists 14 states along with Puerto Rico as supporting this feature, but backend data suggests another state is about to join...

Many people look forward to the day when they no longer need to carry physical identification documents, such as driver's licenses and passports, and can simply present their digital ID directly through iPhone or Apple Watch.

That future may still be far off, but Apple took the first step back in 2021, when the company announced plans to allow iPhone users to add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. To date, 14 states have adopted this feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend data discovered by MacRumors shows that Oklahoma is about to join this list.

We previously provided a detailed tutorial on how to add a driver's license or state ID to the iPhone Wallet app. At that time, we also mentioned that a digital ID may not completely replace physical credentials, so it is still recommended that everyone continue to carry physical identification documents.

That said, at eligible TSA security checkpoints and when verifying age with merchants, the digital version can still effectively protect your privacy. The ID will only confirm that you meet the age requirement, without revealing any personal information, such as your date of birth.
